title: W-2: pasted bytes left on stdin reach the shell, and the passphrase is silently truncated at 1024 bytes
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-2 (high). Both hidden readers stop at the first newline and restore echo without discarding queued input; the secret reader leaves bytes past a refusal unread and the passphrase reader truncates silently at its bound, so the confirm step compares two identically truncated values. No tcflush exists in src/. Files: src/adapters/secret-value.ts, src/adapters/passphrase.ts. One PTY test against the shipped artifact is still owed (the reviewer ran a mirror on a standalone runtime).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The passphrase reader refuses at its bound, as the secret reader does, and never truncates silently
Both readers flush pending input (tcflush TCIFLUSH) on every exit path, success, refusal and Ctrl-C, before restoring echo
A real-PTY test with a multiline paste, a refusal and a Ctrl-C shows no leftover bytes reach the shell
One PTY check is run against the packaged binary

implementationNotes: Opus review at 7b80a75: REQUEST_CHANGES (relay by team-lead, 2026-11-01). HIGH: nothing CI runs proved the real tcflush and an unresolved libc was silent. HIGH if measured: measured on darwin, a paste with a tail past about 1 KB survived a single tcflush and landed after it, echoed. MEDIUM: no negative control recorded. Fixed at 3016a5a: the discard polls until the terminal is quiet for 30 ms then flushes; terminalInputSupport() is read by a test skipped nowhere; an unresolved libc prints one stderr line; three long-tail PTY cases; PTY_PROBE_BINARY runs the suite on a compiled probe (7 of 7 on a native darwin compile). Negative controls: flush no-op fails 7 of 7, drain disabled fails exactly the 3 long-tail cases. LOW: in-code claims reworded to narrows. Residuals: an external signal skips the finally blocks; the 30 ms quiet interval is a heuristic. AC4 on the Linux-cross-built release binary stays with the sitting. Design question routed through team-lead to opum-doc, not decided here: refuse a multi-line paste rather than storing its first line.

Landed: opum-ai/ward-cli#236 (squash 8619d91, 2026-11-01). Opus rounds: 7b80a75 REQUEST_CHANGES, 3016a5a REQUEST_CHANGES (poll revents unread), 2a00d15 APPROVE. Close-blocker evidence, Bun 1.3.14 on macOS arm64: (1) measured leak before the fix: a 6.3 KB tail after the terminator survived a single tcflush (first roughly 1 KB flushed, the rest landed after and was echoed) for secret, passphrase and bound cases; (2) fix: poll until the terminal is quiet for 30 ms then flush, capped at 1.5 s on a monotonic clock; (3) leader timing of 3016a5a: all 7 PTY cases end on a real quiet poll (result 0) at 30.8 to 32.5 ms, paste cases 7 iterations with revents 1 POLLIN, so it is not a tcflush spin; (4) negative controls: flush no-op fails 7 of 7, drain disabled fails exactly the 3 long-tail cases, a bogus libc fails the resolver test, removing the revents error check fails exactly the stop-at-once test, removing the POLLIN check or making a failed poll stop fails exactly the retry case; (5) a compiled probe built with the release build function passes 7 of 7 (PTY_PROBE_BINARY), and /nonexistent fails 7 of 7; CI ran the Linux fifo poll test. Residuals: an external SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP during the blocking read skips the finally blocks (src/cli/guard.ts handles only uncaught errors); the 30 ms quiet interval is a heuristic (iTerm2 Paste Slowly, mosh, ssh over a lossy link, or a paste still streaming past 1.5 s can still leak). AC4 (PTY check on the packaged binary) is held for the sitting, route pending opum-doc (compiled probe only, or plus a manual throwaway-alias check on the release binary); it is NOT ticked here. Multi-line paste design question (refuse rather than store the first line) is with opum-doc through the leader.

Ticked AC1 to AC3 at 2026-11-01 on landed evidence, opum-ai/ward-cli#236 squash 8619d91. AC1: the passphrase reader refuses at 1024 bytes with backup_passphrase_too_large (exactly the bound accepted, the next byte refused, backspace at the bound works; test/passphrase.test.ts, and the PTY bound case). AC2: both readers call the discard on every exit path before echo is restored (test/passphrase.test.ts and test/secret.test.ts order tests, and the real-pty cases for success, refusal and Ctrl-C). AC3: test/pty-residue.test.ts runs a multiline paste, a refused bound passphrase, a Ctrl-C and 6.3 KB long tails on a real pty, 7 of 7, and CI ran the Linux fifo poll test. AC4 stays open for the sitting.

AC4 closed 2026-11-02 from ward-sitting-part3-5b-20261102T174902Z.log (lines 114-126): ward secret set THROWAWAY_PASTE_TEST on the installed v0.1.1 binary, multi-line paste at the hidden prompt whose later lines were echo LEAK-1/2/3; the terminal shows Secret stored (line 115) and no LEAK- line, then the alias was deleted (line 126). The pasted bytes are hidden by design, so the evidence is the absence of LEAK- output and of any command run after the prompt.
finalSummary: W-2 closed: hidden-read exits flush queued input and an over-long passphrase is refused (#236, Opus reviewed). The packaged-binary paste check ran at the operator sitting on 2026-11-02: no LEAK- output and no command run after the prompt. Follow-ups are in WCLI-129.
